title: Logistic Growth S-Curve Explorer
description: Add response delay to logistic growth and watch a smooth S-curve turn into overshoot, then into collapse.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Growth Patterns and Nonlinear Behavior

educational.learningObjective: Given a carrying capacity and a feedback-delay setting, the learner will predict whether a growing quantity settles into a smooth S-curve, overshoots and recovers, or overshoots and collapses.
prerequisites: Knows what a carrying capacity is
learningOutcomes: Predict growth shape from the delay setting
Explain why delay causes overshoot even when the limit is known
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a delay setting and a fragile-limit state and ask them to sketch the resulting curve before running it.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Multi-parameter simulation with three comparison traces
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Systematic variation of one variable (delay) against a fixed reference
pedagogical.feedbackType: Live traces with color-flagged overshoot and a plain-language shape verdict
misconceptionsAddressed: That growth stops neatly at a limit
discussionQuestions: Why does knowing the limit not prevent overshooting it?
Which real limits are fragile, and which recover?
What would shorten the feedback delay in a system you work with?
